calls.head: The Blue Jackets’ defense joins the attack; the Mammoth’s stays home
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Columbus is one of the league’s best and Utah is the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Blue Jackets’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Mammoth’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen, Columbus had 30% and Utah 46%. Coming in, Columbus was at 37% and Utah at 30%.

calls.head: The Mammoth get in close; the Blue Jackets shoot from distance
calls.body: The Mammoth are near the top of the league for shots from in close, at the close-range end; the Blue Jackets are near the bottom of the league, at the long-range end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Mammoth take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Blue Jackets.
calls.nums: Shots from in close: Utah 7th, Columbus 24th
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shots from within 20 feet, Utah had 19% and Columbus 38%. Coming in, Utah was at 31% and Columbus at 30%.

CBJ.head: We had this close to even (49% for Columbus), and it went Utah’s way.

UTA.head: We had this close to even (51% for Utah), and Utah came through.

surprises.head: Columbus got the good looks
surprises.body: Columbus’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: The Mammoth beat the Blue Jackets
paras: Mikhail Sergachev opened the scoring midway through the first. Nick Schmaltz added two goals.
The chances were closer than the score.

items.text: None of the preview’s two calls held.
